strengths: Addressing an important and timely challenge: standard end-to-end GUI agents struggle with interactive CAPTCHAs, while existing CAPTCHA solvers rely on specialized, multi-stage pipelines that cannot perform general GUI navigation.
Well-designed dynamic CAPTCHA simulation environment featuring seven core interaction primitives, incorporating stochastic DOM styling and asset variety to prevent superficial visual memorization.
Principled data curation pipeline that couples expert reasoning generation with rejection-sampled self-correction trajectories, explicitly addressing multi-step error recovery.

Comprehensive empirical validation across held-out synthetic test sets, a real-world benchmark of 26 CAPTCHA variants (zero-shot transfer), and three standard general GUI benchmarks (Android Control, ScreenSpot-V2, and Multimodal-Mind2Web).
Clear ablations confirming the independent utility of both chain-of-thought reasoning supervision and self-correction traces.
weaknesses: Uneven zero-shot transfer on real-world CAPTCHAs: while ReCAP-32B performs well on interactive and spatial tasks, specialized solvers (e.g., Halligan) still substantially outperform it on text-heavy and pattern-matching challenges (e.g., Baidu rotate, Yandex text, MTCaptcha).

Capacity degradation for smaller models: ReCAP-8B exhibits noticeable performance drops on all three general GUI benchmarks (Table 3), indicating that multi-task interference remains a challenge when model capacity is restricted.

Prompting inconsistency in general GUI evaluation: Appendix D.3.2 notes that for ScreenSpot-V2, the prompt for ReCAP-32B was altered by removing the system prompt and modifying user prompt instructions, whereas baseline models were evaluated with original instructions, introducing an evaluation discrepancy.

Real-world behavioral factors (e.g., mouse velocity trajectories, human jitter, timing patterns) are not simulated, as acknowledged by the authors, which modern anti-bot systems increasingly inspect alongside task correctness.

strengths: Addresses an important and practical open problem: native GUI agents frequently get blocked by modern interactive CAPTCHAs, while existing solvers rely on specialized, high-latency search pipelines that cannot handle general computer-use tasks.

A scalable and automated data synthesis framework: creating a procedurally randomized dynamic CAPTCHA engine paired with ground-truth-conditioned expert reasoning generation and student failure-based self-correction trace mining.

Extensive empirical evaluation: demonstrated strong gains on synthetic held-out benchmarks (from ~30% to 81% success rate), substantial zero-shot transfer to real-world CAPTCHA distributions (26 variants), and verification of general GUI capability retention on Android Control, ScreenSpot-V2, and Multimodal-Mind2Web.
Thorough ablation studies that clearly isolate the benefits of both explicit chain-of-thought reasoning supervision (+5.5pp) and self-correction training (+9.0pp).
weaknesses: Mathematical formulation discrepancy in Section 3.3: the text states that reasoning and action tokens are reweighted to assign equal total weight to mitigate length disparity, yet the loss formula defines $\mathcal{L}_{\text{total}} = -\frac{1}{|\mathcal{T}| + |\mathcal{A}|} \left( \lambda_{\text{think}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \log p_\theta + \lambda_{\text{act}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{A}} \log p_\theta \right)$ with $\lambda_{\text{think}} = \lambda_{\text{act}} = 0.5$. Because the individual sums are not normalized by $|\mathcal{T}|$ and $|\mathcal{A}|$, setting equal weights means the longer reasoning tokens still dominate the loss proportionally, contradicting the stated objective.

Evaluation prompt discrepancy: In Appendix D.3.2 (ScreenSpot-V2), the authors note that for ReCAP-32B, the prompt was specifically tuned (removing the system prompt and modifying user prompt format), whereas all other models were evaluated using the standard unmodified prompt. This introduces an uncontrolled evaluation confound.

Noticeable capacity degradation in smaller models: ReCAP-8B exhibits non-trivial degradation on general GUI benchmarks (e.g., dropping over 7% on Android Control Low from 65.80% to 58.60%), indicating that joint CAPTCHA and general GUI co-training induces substantial representational interference at smaller parameter scales.

Transfer limitations on specialized real-world CAPTCHAs: On several challenging real-world types in Table 2 (e.g., baidu/rotate, lemin, geetest/gobang, and yandex/kaleidoscope), ReCAP-32B achieves very low success rates (3% to 33%), lagging significantly behind task-specific search frameworks like Halligan.

strengths: Addresses an important and practical capability gap in native GUI agents, specifically handling interactive, multi-step CAPTCHA challenges without relying on external hand-engineered pipelines or heuristic toolkits.
The dynamic CAPTCHA generation platform features stochastic DOM/styling rendering and asset randomization, which helps mitigate overfitting to static visual layouts.
The rejection-sampling-based self-correction pipeline effectively turns student model failures into explicit error-recovery training data.

Comprehensive empirical validation across synthetic tasks, zero-shot transfer to 26 real-world CAPTCHA variants, and standard GUI agent benchmarks (Android Control, ScreenSpot-V2, and Multimodal-Mind2Web).
Clean ablation studies clearly isolate the relative benefits of chain-of-thought reasoning (+5.5% overall) and self-correction training data (+9.0% overall).
weaknesses: Dual-use security concerns: The paper trains native agents to bypass prominent commercial CAPTCHAs (e.g., Google reCAPTCHA v2, hCaptcha, Arkose) and promises to open-source the model weights and data without discussing mitigation strategies, safe release protocols, or defensive countermeasures.

The data generation methodology relies on hindsight rationalization, where an expert model is provided the ground-truth solution and instructed to 'pretend to find out the error by yourself'. The paper lacks analysis or human evaluation measuring how often this leads to unfaithful reasoning or post-hoc rationalizations.

Severe representational interference and performance degradation on the smaller 8B model when evaluated on general GUI benchmarks (e.g., ScreenSpot-V2 drops from 92.06% to 80.03%, and Android Control drops noticeably), showing that the training mixture is not fully capacity-preserving.

Evaluation on real-world CAPTCHAs tests primarily puzzle/task logic and does not account for modern behavioral biometrics (e.g., mouse trajectories, speed profiles, browser fingerprinting, and interaction timing), which limits the ecological validity of the real-world bypass rates in actual deployment.

strengths: Addresses an important and practical bottleneck in native GUI agent research: solving modern interactive CAPTCHAs directly from pixel observations without breaking the general end-to-end GUI agent paradigm.
Comprehensive data generation pipeline combining procedural dynamic rendering, answer-conditioned rationale generation, and retrospective self-correction traces from student failures.

Thorough empirical evaluation across synthetic dynamic benchmarks, a diverse 26-task real-world CAPTCHA benchmark (Halligan dataset), and four standard general GUI agent benchmarks to evaluate catastrophic forgetting.
Well-designed ablation studies isolating the benefits of chain-of-thought reasoning supervision, self-correction data, and data scaling.
weaknesses: Inconsistent evaluation prompt protocol on general GUI benchmarks: as noted in Appendix D.3.2, the prompt for 32B ReCAP variants was specifically tuned on ScreenSpot-V2 (removing system prompt and adding explicit instructions) whereas baseline models used original ScreenSpot instructions, creating an unfair comparison.

While transfer to real-world CAPTCHAs shows average improvements over base models, performance remains quite low or lagging behind specialized pipelines/frontier models on rotation and complex pattern-matching challenges (e.g., baidu/rotate, geetest/iconcrush, yandex/kaleidoscope).

The security and dual-use risks of training and releasing agents specifically optimized to bypass CAPTCHA defenses warrant a more thorough risk mitigation discussion beyond the brief impact statement.

strengths: Addresses an important and practically relevant problem: enabling native, end-to-end vision-language GUI agents to solve interactive CAPTCHAs without relying on task-specific heuristic pipelines or disjoint external tools.

Well-designed dynamic CAPTCHA generation engine spanning seven representative challenge archetypes with DOM-level and visual asset stochasticity, enabling scalable synthesis with exact ground-truth access.
Effective data curation strategy combining answer-conditioned reasoning traces (rationale bootstrapping) with retrospective self-correction traces derived from student model failures.

Extensive empirical evaluation covering dynamic held-out synthetic test sets, zero-shot transfer across 26 real-world CAPTCHA varieties from the Halligan benchmark, and four standard general GUI agent benchmarks.
Informative ablation studies that clearly demonstrate the distinct value added by chain-of-thought reasoning (+5.5 pp) and self-correction supervision (+9.0 pp) on task completion rates.
weaknesses: Transfer to wild, complex CAPTCHA categories remains uneven: on several challenging real-world types (e.g., baidu/rotate, geetest/gobang, geetest/iconcrush, yandex/kaleidoscope), ReCAP achieves low or near-zero success, trailing specialized search-based frameworks like Halligan and frontier proprietary models.

Evaluation disparity in general GUI benchmarking: Appendix D.3.2 notes that for ScreenSpot-V2, prompts were specifically tuned for the 32B ReCAP variants while baseline models received unmodified instructions, complicating strictly identical comparisons.

The core methodological components—synthetic procedural generation with oracle metadata, STaR-style answer-conditioned rationale bootstrapping, and failure-driven rejection sampling—are largely standard paradigms adapted to the CAPTCHA GUI setting rather than fundamentally new learning algorithms.

The study intentionally abstracts away from continuous behavioral biometrics (e.g., realistic mouse kinematics, timing distributions, and browser fingerprinting), which are increasingly central to modern enterprise bot defense systems.

strengths: The paper addresses an important and practical bottleneck for native GUI agents: handling interactive CAPTCHAs directly within a unified vision-action policy rather than relying on external, slow, or brittle modular pipelines.

The dynamic synthetic CAPTCHA environment is well-engineered, incorporating stochastic rendering and dynamic DOM variation across seven core challenge types to mitigate visual memorization and isolate key interaction primitives (e.g., continuous dragging, precise clicking, OCR under noise).

The automated data generation strategy cleverly leverages ground-truth conditioning to synthesize chain-of-thought traces, combined with a rejection-sampling workflow on student model failures to construct retrospective self-correction data.

Comprehensive empirical validation across multiple dimensions: dynamic synthetic test sets, zero-shot transfer across 26 real-world CAPTCHA variants from the Halligan benchmark, and four standard GUI agent benchmarks (Android Control, ScreenSpot-V2, Mind2Web, UI-Vision) demonstrating retention of general agentic capabilities.
Solid ablation experiments clearly demonstrating the distinct contributions of both chain-of-thought reasoning traces (+5.5 pp) and self-correction traces (+9.0 pp) to task completion rate.
weaknesses: Inconsistent evaluation protocol on general GUI benchmarks: Appendix D.3.2 notes that for ScreenSpot-V2, the prompt for the 32B ReCAP variants was specifically tuned (removing the system prompt and modifying user prompt instructions), whereas all other models used the default prompt without modification, which undermines strict comparability.

Zero-shot transfer to real-world CAPTCHAs is mixed: As reflected in Table 2 and Table 7, performance on several visually complex or unconventional puzzle types (e.g., geetest/gobang, yandex/kaleidoscope, geetest/iconcrush) remains extremely low or near 0%, showing clear boundaries in how well the synthetic primitives generalize to unseen distributions.

Conceptual novelty is relatively incremental: The core training methodologies—answer-conditioned rationale bootstrapping (STaR) and reflection on failed trajectories—are established paradigms in LLM/agent post-training, applied here as a targeted application to GUI CAPTCHA interaction.

Dual-use and safety considerations: While the impact statement touches upon probing security boundaries, automating CAPTCHA bypass directly challenges human-verification mechanisms across web services; a more detailed discussion on mitigation, defensive recommendations, or responsible disclosure/access governance would be beneficial.
